ety.text: Borrowed from Middle French dose, from Late Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis, “a portion prescribed”, literally “a giving”), used by Galen and other Greek physicians to mean an amount of medicine, from δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to give”). Mostly displaced English drench. Doublet of doos.

senses.d: A measured portion of medicine taken at any one time.
ex: Why did he give you only a single 500 mg dose? The correct dosage of this antibiotic is one 500 mg tablet twice a day for 10 days.

senses.d: The quantity of an agent (not always active), substance, or radiation administered or experienced at any one time.
Anything disagreeable that must be taken.
A good measure or lengthy experience of something.
ex: The prospect of becoming a father is a dose of reality that threatens to bring his dream world crashing down.
Don't give a dose to the one you love most. / Give her some marmalade... give her some toast.
It would be very expensive to cure a dose here, as well as unbelievably painful.

senses.d: A cold; a common, viral illness of the nasal passage, sometimes with fever.
To administer a dose (of medicine) to.
ex: "She thought herself broad awake, and I have dosed her with an opiate."

senses.d: To surreptitiously administer a dose of an incapacitating drug (to an unwilling subject); to roofie.
To transmit a venereal disease to.
ex: Sometime back, one of your scarlet sisters dosed me proper.

grp.label: quantity of an agent administered at any one time

ety.text: From Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis). Doublet of dot.

Learned borrowing from Late Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis, “a portion prescribed”, literally “a giving”), from Proto-Hellenic *dótis, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₃tis. Doublet of dote.
Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis).

senses.d: The administration of a medication etc, in a measured amount; dosing.
The addition of a small measured amount of a substance to something, e.g. sugar to wine.
The measured amount so administered or added (the dose), combined with the frequency of administration and the time period for which it is taken.
ex: Why did he give you only a single 500 mg dose? The correct dosage of this antibiotic is one 500 mg tablet twice a day for 10 days.
